touches.text: The only way to the inference host; anything that goes around it is an error. WHY: its two points are to find the cheapest model powerful enough for each request, and to train the graph trees on the results.
TOOLS: base, import_sieve; database client. MACHINES: route, nest.

Claude Code calls Anthropic directly and bypasses the proxy, at least for now. WHY: Anthropic is already the lowest-cost provider for Claude Code, and the trees can learn from CC's logs instead. [Q#95: The usage tool (cairn/tools/usage/usage.py, the orchestrator's usage reading, 11-12) makes one HTTPS GET to api.anthropic.com for the account's usage, by urllib. The sole-path check reads that as a second door to the inference host, and 4 proofs are red on it (measured 2026-11-13, Linux census at 6cbae796b). It calls no model. May usage go on the sole-path allowed list as web_operator did (16.4.4), or should its read go through the inference proxy, or web_operator?]

web_operator may talk on the web by any means: direct HTTP, a browser driven over WebDriver (selenium or similar), or anything like them. So it is on the inference sole-path rule's allowed list (11.4.1). Akien 2026-11-09, answering Q#74: "the web_operator may use direct http calls, browser based calls (via selenium or similar), or any similar mechanism to talk on the web. it is allowed."

Fixit (bug): at BUILDME the ticket names the red it fixes (the proof), and that proof really is red on disk now. The fix may change the test case itself without a ruling: the proof's why names the ticket and says what it tests and why it changed, and names any tooth it removed. At PROVED it is sealed green and hollow-measured.
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.

The RULE 1 check is a path check: code inside device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo (anything not under cairn.devices.bar), except a tool foo publishes (cairn.devices.foo.tools.<x>, its charter saying published_by_device). Inside one device there is one owner, so nothing is checked there. A charter's public_interface describes what the component offers (modules, functions, bus verbs, commands); the check does not read it. Akien 2026-11-09 (Q#77): "wouldn't it be easier (for the python code anyway) to see if the imports do not include other device paths?"
